transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 10:00 AM - 10:45 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (NexaHealth CTO), Priya Rao (NexaHealth ML), Martin Gomez (NexaHealth IT), Aisha Khan (NexaHealth Security)

Topics: onboarding status, access & networking, security questions (KMS/SOC2), benchmark plan, next steps

---
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah, um, quick agenda — onboarding progress, access setup, env readiness, and then we'll lock down next steps. Sound good?
[00:14] Jordan Lee: Yep, all good from our side.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Thanks Alex. We got a few updates on the staging environment.
[00:22] Martin Gomez: Morning. I, uh, set up the staging VPC last week. Still working on the IP allowlist for third-party egress.
[00:29] Alex Chen: Great. For the benchmark we need a service account with token-based access and the allowlist, and then we'll run the Dedicated pool test. Samira, I'll hand to you for the tech details.
[00:41] Samira Gupta: Cool. For the POC we recommend two runs: a 95th percentile latency run with representative prompts and a throughput run to validate batching. We can run against Hosted first, but Dedicated gives more predictable results — especially for KV cache heavy workloads.
[01:02] Priya Rao: Quick question: our prompts are mostly short medical note summarization, so the token length is low but concurrency is high. We're targetting around 5k requests per day with spikes in the morning. Latency target is 200-300ms p95 if possible.
[01:20] Samira Gupta: That aligns with what we've seen — depends on batching and cold starts. On Dedicated we can pin model variant and keep warm instances to avoid stalls. Also worth considering quantization and lighter model variants if cost is an issue.
[01:36] Aisha Khan: From security, we need to confirm key management. Do you support customer-managed keys? HSM? How are logs retained? SOC2 scope?
[01:45] Alex Chen: Yes, we support KMS integrations, customer-managed keys, and can integrate with HSM via our Private deployment. SOC2 report is available — I'll share that. Log retention is configurable; we can provide audit logs for the pilot.
[01:58] Aisha Khan: Okay, can you send the network diagram showing where the egress happens? We need to make sure PHI isn't leaving our region unintentionally.
[02:07] Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll add region routing notes and the fallback behavior if a Dedicated node is unavailable. We can also pin region to us-west-2 for the pilot.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: One more infra detail — we run strict egress rules and the ops team wants the Redwood IP ranges to be allowlisted rather than a broad outbound rule. Martin is on the call.
[02:28] Martin Gomez: Yeah, I'll set up the allowlist. Need the list from you Alex.
[02:32] Alex Chen: I'll send the IP list after the call. Also, we'll need a service account key; Martin, can you create that in staging and grant it minimal privileges?
[02:42] Martin Gomez: Yep, I can do that.
[02:45] Samira Gupta: For the benchmark specifics — we'll run three profiles: 1) short prompt latency (p95), 2) batch throughput with concurrency, 3) end-to-end integration test with your pre/post-processing. For the KV cache tests, we may see different tail latencies if the cache misses are frequent.
[03:05] Priya Rao: I suspect most requests will hit the same prefixes, so caching should help. But we'll provide a dataset so you can tune cache TTLs.
[03:13] Samira Gupta: Perfect. Also, quick note — transcription, sorry — the auto-transcription sometimes writes 'kay vee cash' in the notes, you'll see typos in our shared doc.
[03:22] Diego Morales: (laughs) classic.
[03:24] Jordan Lee: On the timeline, we want the initial benchmark results within two weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[03:30] Samira Gupta: Yes, if we get service account and allowlist this week and dataset by Monday, we can run hosted tests immediately and Dedicated the week after.
[03:39] Alex Chen: I'll aim to share SOC2 and network diagram by EOD 2026-03-28. Samira to schedule the benchmark for week of 2026-04-06. Martin to provide service account and allowlist by 2026-03-29. Priya to upload dataset by 2026-03-30.
[03:56] Aisha Khan: Also want to confirm data residency — logs and any cached persisted data remain in our region.
[04:02] Samira Gupta: Yes, we can pin to region and ensure any cache persistence follows region routing. We'll note that in the runbook.
[04:09] Jordan Lee: Cost question — do you have estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted for our workload? Ballpark numbers are fine.
[04:16] Alex Chen: We will send a cost model. Generally, Dedicated lowers per-token unit cost at steady state, but Hosted is easier to start. We'll include batching and quantization options in the estimate.
[04:27] Priya Rao: For evaluation, we also want to capture output quality. We'll include a small eval set to check for hallucinations and medical accuracy.
[04:35] Samira Gupta: Great — please include expected metrics and any pass/fail criteria. We'll wire that into our regression checks.
[04:43] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[04:45] Diego Morales: Quick note — I've attached the onboarding checklist link in the calendar invite and the security pack in the follow-up.
[04:52] Alex Chen: Awesome, thanks Diego. Okay, recap of next steps and action items...
[04:57] Alex Chen: Action items: Alex will send SOC2 + network diagram; Samira schedules benchmark; Martin creates service account + allowlist; Priya uploads dataset. We'll reconvene after initial benchmark.
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:13] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[05:15] Aisha Khan: Thanks.
[05:17] Alex Chen: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: transcription shows occasional speaker label mismatches and typos (e.g., "kay vee cash" for KV cache). Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding checklist (calendar link), SOC2 + security pack (to be shared), benchmark spreadsheet (to be scheduled).
